messages:
anya: noticed spike in GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1-b around 03:10 UTC. Mostly tiny-gang training jobs getting bounced.
marc: same here. Any network alerts or node drains?
kai: root cause looks like conntrack overflow on 2 racks -> NIC rebinds -> kubelet flapped NotReady -> scheduler preempt churn.
liz: which taint was applied?
anya: taint=nic-unavailable:NoSchedule applied by node-watchdog when NIC rebind failed.
sre-tim: sample logs:
``n03:09:34 kube-scheduler WARN Preempting pod gpu-small-1 for gpu-batch-high
03:09:36 kubelet INFO eviction threshold reached, gracefulTerminationSeconds=30
```
marc: 30s is too short for GPU warmpool jobs. They lose KV cache and requeue hot-loop.
kai: we have per-pool grace overrides but ap-southeast1 cluster missed the update due to label-sync delay (api-server latency).
liz: quick mitigation: canary bump grace to 120s for pods with label workload=gpu in az ap-southeast1-b. Also add a 60s requeue-backoff on recently-evicted pods to avoid immediate rescheduling.
ops-bot: patch request queued for canary: set evictionGraceOverride selector=workload=gpu graceSeconds=120 scope=az:ap-southeast1-b
deploy-bot: applying canary in ~2m. Adding requeue-backoff controller=true. :gear:
sre-tim: also propose a safety: if node reports NIC down >300s, force eviction to avoid long-tail stuck pods (cap knob).
anya: agreed. Run canary 2h, monitor evictions/sec, warmpool warmup latency, and cost delta. Report back after 2h. :thumbsup:
